description:
Starfruit (Averrhoa carambola) is extremely toxic to cats and must be kept away from them at all times. The entire fruit, including the flesh and juice, contains dangerous compounds that can cause severe and rapid-onset illness, even in very small amounts.

The fruit contains high levels of soluble calcium oxalates and a neurotoxin called caramboxin. When a cat eats starfruit, the soluble oxalates are absorbed into the bloodstream, where they bind to calcium. This causes a sudden, dangerous drop in the body's calcium levels and leads to the formation of crystals that cause severe, acute kidney failure. The caramboxin can also cause serious neurological symptoms.

Any amount of starfruit ingestion is a medical emergency. Symptoms can appear quickly and include vomiting, drooling, weakness, tremors, changes in thirst or urination, and seizures. If you suspect your cat has eaten even a tiny piece of starfruit, please contact a veterinarian or an emergency animal hospital immediately.
name: Starfruit
safetyNotes: Toxic compounds: caramboxin (neurotoxin) and high soluble oxalates; the entire fruit is toxic
Mechanism: caramboxin inhibits GABA synthesis, causing neurological excitation; oxalates precipitate as calcium oxalate crystals in kidney tubules
Symptoms: vomiting, hiccups, agitation, confusion, seizures, acute kidney failure; onset within 1–5 hours
There is no known safe amount of starfruit for cats — even a small piece or juice can cause toxicity
Any starfruit ingestion is a veterinary emergency

symptoms.name: Vomiting, drooling, and loss of appetite
Increased thirst and urination, dehydration, bloody urine, and eventually reduced urine output or a complete inability to urinate
